stem.en: Rural development mainly means:

options.en: Action to develop the areas that are lagging behind in the overall development of the village economy
Raising only the output of food grains

explanation.en: Rural development focuses on action for the development of areas that are lagging behind in the overall development of the village economy.

stem.en: Which of the following is NOT a key area of rural development?

options.en: Infrastructure such as electricity, irrigation and roads

explanation.en: Human resources, land reforms, local productive resources, infrastructure and poverty alleviation are the key areas. Stock market trading is not one of them.

stem.en: Infrastructure needed for rural development includes:

options.en: Electricity, irrigation, credit, marketing and transport facilities

explanation.en: Rural infrastructure covers electricity, irrigation, credit, marketing, transport (village roads), agricultural research and extension, and information.

stem.en: According to Mahatma Gandhi, the real progress of India meant:

options.en: Growth of big industrial cities only
Mainly the development of the villages

explanation.en: Gandhi held that India's real progress meant not just the growth of urban industrial centres but mainly the development of the villages.

solution.en: Gandhi held that India's real progress meant not just the growth of urban industrial centres but mainly the development of the villages.

stem.en: A reason given for the slowdown of agricultural growth in India after 1991 is:

options.en: A rise in public investment in agriculture
A decline in public investment in agriculture, such as irrigation and infrastructure
Too many farmers moving to organic farming
A fall in the rural population to zero

explanation.en: Public investment in agriculture declined after 1991, and with weak infrastructure and few alternative jobs, agricultural growth slowed.

stem.en: NABARD was set up in:

explanation.en: The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) was set up in 1982 as the apex body coordinating rural financing.

stem.en: The apex institution that coordinates the activities of all institutions in the rural financing system is:

explanation.en: NABARD coordinates the rural financing system, which includes commercial banks, regional rural banks, cooperatives and land development banks.

stem.en: Self-help groups (SHGs) mainly help the rural poor by:

options.en: Pooling small savings of members and giving them small loans at reasonable interest

explanation.en: SHGs encourage thrift: members save small amounts and the pooled fund lends to members. This is micro-credit.

stem.en: Farmers need credit mainly because:

options.en: They have a regular monthly salary
There is a long gap between sowing the crop and getting income from the harvest
Crops are always sold before sowing
They do not need seeds or fertiliser

explanation.en: Because of the long gestation period between sowing and harvest, farmers borrow for seeds, fertilisers and implements, and for family needs.

solution.en: Because of the long gestation period between sowing and harvest, farmers borrow for seeds, fertilisers and implements, and for family needs.

stem.en: A major problem of formal rural credit institutions has been:

options.en: Poor recovery of loans and high default rates
Lending only to big industries by law

explanation.en: Formal institutions have struggled with poor recovery and high default rates, and they have not fully replaced informal lenders.

stem.en: Agricultural marketing includes:

options.en: Only advertising farm products on TV
Only selling crops in the village
Assembling, storage, processing, transportation, packaging, grading and distribution of farm produce

explanation.en: Agricultural marketing is the whole process from assembling the produce to grading, storing, processing, transporting and distributing it.

stem.en: The minimum support price (MSP) policy is meant to:

options.en: Fix the maximum price consumers pay
Safeguard farmers' income against a fall in the price of their produce

explanation.en: MSP assures farmers a minimum price for crops such as wheat and rice, protecting them from sharp price falls.

stem.en: Rythu Bazars, where farmers sell directly to consumers, are found in:

explanation.en: Rythu Bazars are in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. Uzhavar Sandies are in Tamil Nadu, Apni Mandis in Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan, and the Hadaspar Mandi in Pune.

stem.en: Buffer stocks of wheat and rice in India are maintained by the:

explanation.en: The Food Corporation of India procures and keeps buffer stocks of wheat and rice, which are distributed through the public distribution system.

solution.en: The Food Corporation of India procures and keeps buffer stocks of wheat and rice, which are distributed through the public distribution system.

stem.en: A "distress sale" by farmers means:

options.en: Selling through government agencies at MSP
Selling at high prices in the off-season
Selling produce soon after harvest at low prices because they lack storage and need money

explanation.en: Without storage and credit, farmers often must sell immediately after harvest when prices are lowest. This is a distress sale.

stem.en: The "Golden Revolution" refers to rapid growth in:

explanation.en: The period 1991–2003 of rapid growth in horticulture (fruits, vegetables, flowers, spices, plantation crops) is called the Golden Revolution.

stem.en: Operation Flood is associated with:

explanation.en: Operation Flood organised milk producers into cooperatives and is linked with the White Revolution in dairying.

stem.en: Diversification of agricultural activities means:

options.en: Changing the cropping pattern and shifting workforce to allied activities and the non-farm sector

explanation.en: It has two aspects: change in cropping pattern, and a shift of workers from crop farming to allied activities (livestock, poultry, fisheries) and non-farm work.

stem.en: Diversification is needed in rural areas mainly because:

options.en: Agriculture already gives work throughout the year everywhere
Depending only on crop farming is risky and leaves many without work in the non-crop season

explanation.en: Farming depends on the monsoon and gives little work in the rabi season in unirrigated areas, so other activities reduce risk and provide gainful work.

solution.en: Farming depends on the monsoon and gives little work in the rabi season in unirrigated areas, so other activities reduce risk and provide gainful work.

stem.en: Which of the following is a non-farm activity in rural areas?

explanation.en: Agro-processing, food processing, leather, pottery, handicrafts and tourism are non-farm activities.

stem.en: Organic farming avoids the use of:

explanation.en: Organic farming relies on organic inputs such as compost, manure and bio-pest control, and avoids synthetic chemicals.

stem.en: Which is a benefit of organic farming?

options.en: It substitutes costly inputs with cheaper locally produced organic inputs
Its produce always has a longer shelf life
It always gives higher yields from the first year

explanation.en: Organic farming uses locally made inputs (compost, manure), which are cheaper, and its produce has export demand and is healthier.

stem.en: A limitation of organic farming is that:

options.en: Its yields may be lower, at least in the early years

explanation.en: Yields from organic farms are often lower in the initial years, and small and marginal farmers may find it hard to adopt.

stem.en: The first state in India declared fully organic is:

explanation.en: Sikkim was declared India's first fully organic state in 2016.

solution.en: Sikkim was declared India's first fully organic state in 2016.

stem.en: Sustainable development means development that:

options.en: Meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs
Uses up resources as fast as possible

explanation.en: Sustainable development meets the needs of the present generation without reducing the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Self-help groups have helped reduce the dependence of the rural poor on informal moneylenders.
Reason (R): SHGs pool the small savings of their members and lend to members at reasonable rates of interest.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both are true, and R explains A: SHG micro-credit gives the poor an alternative to costly informal loans.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Organic farming can generate more employment in rural areas.
Reason (R): Organic farming uses large quantities of chemical fertilisers.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is true: organic farming is labour intensive. R is false: organic farming avoids chemical fertilisers.

stem.en: What is Ramesh's share in the consumer's rupee?

explanation.en: Farmer's share = 12 ÷ 40 × 100 = 30%. The other 70% goes to transport, middlemen and their margins.

passage.en: Ramesh grows tomatoes near Kolar. He has no cold storage, so he sells his crop through a commission agent soon after harvest at ₹12 per kg. The same tomatoes reach consumers in Bengaluru at ₹40 per kg after passing through a wholesaler and a retailer. His neighbour sells part of her crop directly to buyers at a farmers' market.

stem.en: Which measure would most directly raise the share that farmers like Ramesh receive?

options.en: More commission agents in the chain
Direct farmer-to-consumer markets such as Rythu Bazars and Uzhavar Sandies
A higher retail price in Bengaluru
Selling the whole crop on the day of harvest

explanation.en: Direct markets cut out middlemen, so the farmer gets a larger part of what the consumer pays. Cold storage would also help him avoid distress sales.

passage.en: Ramesh grows tomatoes near Kolar. He has no cold storage, so he sells his crop through a commission agent soon after harvest at ₹12 per kg. The same tomatoes reach consumers in Bengaluru at ₹40 per kg after passing through a wholesaler and a retailer. His neighbour sells part of her crop directly to buyers at a farmers' market.

stem.en: Match: (i) Golden Revolution (ii) White Revolution (iii) Blue Revolution with (a) fisheries (b) horticulture (c) milk production.

explanation.en: Golden: horticulture; White: milk (Operation Flood); Blue: fisheries.

solution.en: Golden: horticulture; White: milk (Operation Flood); Blue: fisheries.

stem.en: Kudumbashree is:

options.en: A cold storage chain in Karnataka
A crop insurance scheme of Punjab
A women-oriented, community-based poverty reduction programme in Kerala built around thrift and credit

explanation.en: Kudumbashree in Kerala organises poor women into thrift-and-credit groups and is a well-known SHG-based poverty reduction programme.

stem.en: Statement I: NABARD was set up in 1982 to coordinate rural financing. Statement II: Regional Rural Banks were set up only after NABARD was formed. Choose the correct option.

options.en: Statement I is true, Statement II is false
Statement I is false, Statement II is true

explanation.en: NABARD dates from 1982, so I is true. Regional Rural Banks were set up from 1975, before NABARD, so II is false.
